name: Vora Aegis
summary: A local AI appliance you own: an assistant called a Guardian builds an encrypted database of your digital life on the device and runs open models on it. Announced for Spring 2027; reservations only.

sources.title: Vora Aegis Reservation, $2,499 Super Early Bird

claims.value: A desktop appliance you own that runs open models on-device, split so the layer holding your data has no unrestricted internet access and the internet-facing layer holds no private data
Acts from its own appliance through connected accounts and a secure browser; it does not control your Mac or PC, and no remote interface onto the device's own screen is described
A secure browser runs errands on the internet from the internet-facing layer, which holds no private data
No ambient listening by design; the company contrasts Aegis with always-on speakers and says you talk to it through the app when you choose. A voice interface is not described
Runs errands sent out to the internet and keeps a current brief in the app; scheduled or event-triggered routines are not specified
claims.shortValue: Errands and a brief; triggers not specified

claims.value: No native desktop app is described; deeper work such as connecting accounts happens in the web app from a laptop
claims.shortValue: Web app, not a native desktop app

claims.value: A phone app pairs the device and handles quick questions and notifications; iPhone and Android availability is not separately specified, and full phone-desktop parity is described as growing after launch
A phone app and a web app. The device itself has no screen or keyboard
Ships running Gemma 4 26B entirely on the device; the specifications cite over 100 tokens per second for open models of that size, naming Qwen 3.6 35B and Ornith 1.5 35B
The model is the owner's to choose and can be replaced with newer open models as they are released
Bought outright; the company states the machine runs the full experience with no subscription, and all three optional plans are future development that will not be available at launch

US$2,499 Super Early Bird reservation with a US$50 refundable deposit; a published ladder runs to US$2,799 Early Bird and US$2,999 retail. Optional post-launch plans are US$20/month Guardian Care, US$20/month Aegis Pro and US$100/month Aegis Pro+
The specifications state open source top to bottom, and the company says updates are checked against published source; no public repository is linked from the site, so the code could not be inspected
claims.shortValue: Open source stated; no repository linked

claims.value: Runs on the owner's appliance on EnclaveOS, a hardened security-first operating system. Account data flows from the provider straight to the device rather than through a Vora server. Optional frontier-model credits would send only approved content off-device, and are not available at launch

Sign-in keys for connected accounts are held on the device, and the Harpē security module holds the encryption keys plus a hardware wallet for payments; a general-purpose password manager is not described
Anything consequential is drafted and waits for approval before it is sent; NFC tap-to-verify provides multi-signature confirmation of sensitive data and of payments above a threshold the owner sets

One encrypted database on the device holds mail, messages, photos, calendar, files, financial and health accounts; conversation history imports from ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini. One owner per device, with household modes not yet offered
Everything exports in open formats at any time, and connected data can be deleted from Settings; the company states there is no lock-in and the device keeps working without its servers

Harpē, a hardware security module with dual secure elements, holds keys locally; the split-agent design is presented as structural protection against prompt-injection exfiltration. No training on customer data, signed updates verified against published source with automatic rollback, and a recovery phrase the company states it cannot recover

Not yet available. Reservations only: the US$50 Super Early Bird deposit holds one of 200 units, refundable until the unit ships. Aegis is stated to ship Spring 2027, launching in the United States, Canada and the European Union

platforms.detail: A web app is described for connecting accounts and managing settings; it ships with the device in Spring 2027
A phone app pairs the device and handles quick questions and notifications; iPhone and Android are not separately specified, and it ships with the device in Spring 2027

hardware.name: Vora Aegis
hardware.detail: A compact desktop appliance, 225mm x 185mm x 50mm and 2.2 lbs, with an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395, Radeon 8060S, 64GB unified memory, a 1TB SSD expandable through two M.2 sockets, and the Harpē security module. The device is required: it is the product. Announced to ship Spring 2027, and the site states its images are renders of the production enclosure

access.detail: Not yet available. Reservations only: the US$50 Super Early Bird deposit holds one of 200 units, refundable until the unit ships. Aegis is stated to ship Spring 2027, launching in the United States, Canada and the European Union

onYourComputer.detail: Acts from its own appliance through connected accounts and a secure browser; it does not control your Mac or PC, and no remote interface onto the device's own screen is described

agentComputer.detail: The Aegis appliance is the agent's computer and it has no screen or keyboard; you reach it through the phone and web apps rather than viewing its desktop.

whileYouAreOff.detail: The appliance does the work and stays on by itself; your phone pairs with it and is not what runs the models.

worksWithoutVendor.detail: The company states the appliance keeps working without its servers, needs no subscription, and cannot be switched off by an activation server.

remoteDisable.detail: No activation server can disable it; the owner holds the keys and the machine runs without Vora.

dataAfterExit.detail: Everything exports in open formats at any time, with no lock-in or exit fee described.
